what_matters.head: Alphabet fell 12.3% on Thursday, about 8 times its usual daily move, on volume 3.6 times normal. It was the first full session after its Q3 results.
what_matters.detail: Revenue rose 25% to $127.6B, about what analysts expected, and Google Cloud more than doubled to $30.7B. Search and other Google services grew 11%. Free cash flow was minus $9.1B, after $51.4B of spending on data centres and equipment in the quarter. The company kept its 2026 spending plan of $195–205B and said spending will rise significantly in 2027. Reported earnings per share were $2.12, against about $3.02 expected; that figure includes an $8.7B paper loss on its equity holdings. Yahoo Finance's live coverage reported nearly $500B of market value lost, the worst day in the company's history.

what_matters.tag_note: Intel · Amazon · after Thursday's US close
what_matters.head: Intel fell 23% in after-hours trading and Amazon 7.3%, after results that came out after Thursday's close. Neither move is in Thursday's US prices.
what_matters.detail: Intel: Q3 revenue was $16.5B, inside its $15.8–16.8B forecast, and earnings per share $0.52 against $0.40 expected. Its Q4 forecast is $15.0–16.0B with earnings per share of $0.25; one analyst on the call put it about $1.8B below what Wall Street expected. The company expects PC units to fall about 12% in 2026 and about 10% in 2027, and blamed scarce, expensive memory. A shutdown at its Israel factory will cost about $300M of revenue in Q4 and about the same in Q1. Amazon: revenue was $201.9B against $202.1B expected, and earnings per share $1.89 against $1.96. AWS grew 39% to $46.0B. Its Q4 sales forecast of $240–247B has a midpoint below the $244.3B analysts expected. It kept its 2026 spending plan at about $220B; free cash flow over the last 12 months was minus $42.4B.

what_matters.head: SK Hynix was down 7.3% and Samsung 5.0% by 12:05 SGT, as Thursday's US tech selling spread to Asia.
what_matters.detail: A Dow Jones report on MarketScreener said the Kospi fell 5.2% and that Korea Exchange briefly paused trading after index futures fell more than 5%. Samsung extended its Thursday fall after its Q3 results. Investing.com says the Bank of Japan kept its rate at 1.25% today; Japan's Nikkei fell 2.8%, led by chip stocks.

after_data.text: Fiscal Q1 revenue was $11.0B, above the company's $10.30–10.80B forecast, and gross margin 85.1%, above its 83–85% range. Its forecast for next quarter is $12.2–12.6B. The shares fell 3.8% after hours. About 50% of its fiscal 2027 output is under long-term agreements.
Q3 revenue was $73.4M and adjusted earnings per share $0.41, against $0.31 expected (FactSet, via MT Newswires). The shares fell 6.9% after hours.
AMD fell 6.8% after hours as Intel's forecast pulled chip stocks down after the close; Reuters had it down 4% and Broadcom down 2% when it wrote. AMD reports on Tuesday.

recent.headline: Alphabet fell 12.3% on Thursday, about 8 times its usual daily move, on volume 3.6 times normal. It was the first full session after its Q3 results.
Alphabet fell 9.8% in after-hours trading after its profit came in below forecasts. Microsoft rose 2.9% after hours on faster cloud growth. Neither move is in Wednesday's US prices.
SK Hynix's third-quarter revenue passed 100 trillion won for the first time, and operating profit beat forecasts. By 12:05 SGT its shares were up 10.5%, 2.2× their usual day.
Bloom Energy fell 11.2% on Friday, 2.2× its usual day, even though its third-quarter results beat forecasts and it raised its 2026 revenue forecast.
Chip stocks fell hard on Thursday: the chip fund lost 6.8%, 2.7× its usual day, and the Nasdaq 2.6%, its biggest one-day fall since early June.
